To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ultradispersed SnO2 nanocystals anchored on graphene sheets are a fascinating negative electrode for sodium ion capacitors.

ultradispersed SnO2 nanocystals anchored on graphene exhibit surface-controlled pseudocacitive Na storage, and this material can be utilized as an attractive negative electrode material in quasi-solid-state Na-ion capacitors.

ultradispersed SnO2 nanosheets anchored on graphene nanowalls (GNS-SnO2 NWs) exhibit surface-dominated pseudocapacitative Na storage behavior and are further used as the negative electrode in a quasi-solid Na-ion capacitor with a high energy density of 70.4 Wh kg-1 and an outstanding rate capability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a high-performance Na ion capacitor based on the pseudocapacitor-type ultradispersed SnO2 nanocatalysts.
the development of a new type of pseudocapacitor electrode material with a high specific capacity for sodium storage, which is based on ultradisperse SnO2 nanosurfaces.
the development of ultradispersed SnO2 nanocatalysts for Na storage and the application of the resulting SnO2/graphene composite in quasi-solid-state Na-ion capacitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ultradispersed SnO2 nanocrys­tals anchored on graphene nanowalls exhibit a surface-controlled redox reac­tion-based pseudocapacity for the Na+ storage.
this work will enrich the development of electrode materials with surface-controlled redox reactions for Na-ion capacitors.
the ultradispersed SnO2 NCs/GNS composite is a promising negative electrode material for high-performance quasi-solid state Na ion capacitor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that ultradispersed SnO2 nanosurfaces with highly reactive {221}-facets can be used to store sodium ions.

we have successfully developed a new type of pseudocapacitor electrode materials with high specific capacity and excellent cyclability, which can be used for high-performance quasi-solid Na ion capacitors, and the work will be beneficial for the development of electrode materials with surface redox reaction-based Na storage for Na ion batteries, Na ion capacitors and other electrochemical energy storage devices.

the ultradispersed SnO2 nanosurfaces anchored on graphene nanowalls can reversibly store sodium ions through both a pseudocapacitative reaction and a diffusion-controlled alloying reaction, which are favorable for the development of high-performance quasi-solid state sodium-ion capacitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ultradispersed SnO2 nanocystals anchored on graphene can store Na ions through surface-controlled pseudocacitive reaction and diffusion-limited alloy reaction, which can be utilized as a fascinating anode material in a quasi-Solid-state Na-ion capacitors with excellent electrochemical performance.

the ultradispersed SnO2 nanosheets anchored on graphene nanoflakes can reversibly store large amount of Na ions through both surface-controlled pseudocacitive reaction and diffusion-controlled alloying reaction.
the pseudocapacitor-like SnO2 nanosurfaces provide a novel electrode material with fast Na storage and excellent cyclabilty for quasi-solid-state Na-ion capacitors.
